stem: In the figure, line \(PQ\) passes through vertex \(A\) of triangle \(ABC\) and is parallel to \(\overline{BC}\). What is the value of \(x\)?
solution: Angles \(PAB\), \(BAC\), and \(CAQ\) together form a straight angle along line \(PQ\).

explanation.A: Correct. The three angles at \(A\) form a straight line: \(x = 180 - 57 - 68 = 55\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is \(180 - 68\), which leaves out the \(57^{\circ}\) angle.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This assumes \(x^{\circ}\) equals the neighboring \(68^{\circ}\) angle; nothing makes these two angles equal.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is \(57 + 68\), the sum of the two given angles, not what is left of the straight angle.

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'A': 'A', 'C': 'B', 'B': 'C', 'D': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'A', 'B': 'C', 'C': 'B', 'D': 'D'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert P['P'][1]==P['Q'][1] and P['B'][1]==P['C'][1]
assert abs(ang('P','A','B')-57)<0.1 and abs(ang('C','A','Q')-68)<0.1
ans=180-57-68
assert abs(ang('B','A','C')-ans)<0.1
assert value(choices[answer])==ans==55
assert all(value(choices[k])!=ans for k in choices if k!=answer)
